title: Vanilla Cream Éclairs with Chocolate Glaze
summary: Crisp choux fingers filled with a light vanilla pastry cream and dipped in a glossy dark chocolate glaze.
equipment: piping bag with 1.5 cm plain nozzle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate (60-70% cocoa solids), finely chopped
ingredients.note: check the label for soya and milk

steps.title: Pastry cream
steps.text: whisk the yolks, sugar, cornflour and salt smooth, then whisk in the milk. Cook over medium heat, whisking, until it thickens, then let it bubble gently 1 min; it will pass 85 °C. Strain, whisk in the butter and vanilla, cover the surface and chill 2 h.

steps.title: Choux
steps.text: heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan) and line the tray. Bring the butter, water, milk, sugar and salt to the boil, tip in the flour and beat over low heat 1-2 min until it forms a smooth ball. Cool 4 min, then beat in the eggs a little at a time until the paste is glossy and drops slowly from the spoon in a V. Cooking the paste dries it so it holds more egg and puffs well.

steps.title: Pipe
steps.text: pipe 12 fingers 12 cm long and 2.5 cm wide, 5 cm apart.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: bake 30-35 min, without opening the door for the first 20 min, until deep golden and light. Pierce each end with the skewer and cool on the rack. Opening the door early lets steam out and the pastry can collapse.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: whip the cold cream to firm peaks, beat the chilled pastry cream smooth and fold the two together. Make 2 small holes underneath each éclair and pipe in the cream until it feels heavy.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: bring the cream and golden syrup to a simmer, pour over the chocolate, wait 3 min and stir smooth. Dip the top of each éclair in the glaze, let the excess drip off and set 20 min.

tips: A common mistake is underbaking; pale éclairs go soft and flat as they cool.
Add the last of the egg slowly, as you may not need it all.
Fill no more than 2 hours before serving so the pastry stays crisp.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Filled éclairs keep in the fridge for up to 1 day. Unfilled shells freeze for 1 month; recrisp at 160 °C (140 °C fan) for 5 min.
